lecons.html:
A disciple of Christ is first of all a person who is born of God, follows Christ and lives as he himself lived (Luke 6:40).

To be a mature disciple of Christ, you must necessarily:

  • Be a child of God
  • Know the Gospel of Christ
  • Know how to enjoy the benefits of the new covenant
  • Be prepared for persecutions and tribulations
  • Carry your cross
  • Hold on to the hope of eternal life
  • Stay free
  • Understand and carry out your role as an ambassador of Christ

You are certainly a person who believes you are a Christian; otherwise you would not find yourself in this Builder class. But then, are you a child of God? Have you experienced the new birth? We invite you to answer this fundamental question by taking the following spiritual DNA test.

What is the purpose of a spiritual DNA test? Well, it is to meet the requirement of the apostle Paul: “Examine your own selves, whether you are in the faith. Test your own selves. Or don’t you know about your own selves, that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless indeed you are disqualified.” (2 Cor 13:5)

Since he is an apostle of Jesus Christ and received authority to teach us what is necessary and essential for life in Christ, and since his testimony is backed by the Holy Spirit, we need to test ourselves to be sure we belong to the faith, that is, that we have the new birth and eternal life.

The test presents a few questions based on the Word of God. You must answer the questions sincerely and then work out your result as shown. There are no right answers. There are only your answers, which will let you know where you stand and how to grow. The answers must be Yes or No. Nothing more. If there is a “but” attached to your Yes, it is definitely a NO. A no is simply a no. You must finish answering the questions of all the levels of the test before you start looking at the results. The indicators are there to help you read your results.

After the tests and the results, you will find some guidance to move forward with God in the right direction, whatever your result.

The test of belief: faith

1 John says: “Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him.” (1 John 5:1). Genuine faith in Jesus proves that God is your Father (Gal 3:26).

Faith starts with facts. The apostles lived and worked with Jesus for years. They saw him, heard him and touched him. They bore witness, and this is recorded in the gospels and the letters of the New Testament. John, speaking as an apostle of Christ and author of Scripture, says: “We are of God. He who knows God listens to us. He who is not of God doesn’t listen to us. By this we know the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.” (1 John 4:6). Answer the following questions:

Indicator 1

  • Do you believe the Word of the apostles without reservation?
  • Do you believe the Bible without reservation?
  • In the first letter of John, the Bible says that Jesus is “the Christ” (5:1), “the Son of God” (4:15). “We know that the Son of God has come, and has given us an understanding, that we know him who is true, and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.” (5:20). He “has come in the flesh” (4:2) to die as “And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world.” (2:2) and “He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. To this end the Son of God was revealed: that he might destroy the works of the devil.” (3:8). Do you believe this about Jesus?
  • Do you believe that Jesus Christ rose bodily from the dead? (Rom 10:9)
  • Do you believe that Jesus is the only solution, the only savior of the world that God has given? (Acts 4:12)
  • Do you believe that the Blood of Jesus Christ is enough to pay for your sins? (1 John 1:7, 2:2)
  • Do you believe that only because of Jesus, God forgives your sins and does not bring them up again? (1 John 2:12)
  • Do you take delight in Jesus?
  • Do you trust in his love?
  • Is Jesus enough for you?

Indicator 2

  • In your opinion, was Jesus simply a good man, one wise man among many, a founder of a religion like any other, simply a great teacher, a mere prophet?
  • Do you think Jesus was not God?
  • Do you think Jesus is not enough for you?
  • Do you think something must be added to faith in Christ?
  • Do you think it is possible to be right with God and have eternal life without Christ?

The test of attitude: love

“Beloved, let’s love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves has been born of God, and knows God. He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love. … We know and have believed the love which God has for us. God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.” (1 John 4:7-8, 16). If you have the kind of life of God in you, you will have the kind of love of God. You will love God and the people around you in spite of differences. In fact, our attitude toward God can be measured by our attitude toward others. “If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen? This commandment we have from him, that he who loves God should also love his brother.” (1 John 4:20-21). Answer the following questions:

Indicator 3

  • Do you love God?
  • Are you excited by the things that relate to God and glorify him?
  • Do you love the people around you?
  • Do you love true Christians despite their differences from you?

Indicator 4

  • Do you hate people for no reason? Do you hate people just because of the color of their skin, their physical appearance, the way they laugh…?

The test of action: holiness

If the life of God is in you, your behavior will show it. John says: “If you know that he is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him.” (1 John 2:29). “We know that whoever is born of God doesn’t sin, but he who was born of God keeps himself, and the evil one doesn’t touch him.” (1 John 5:18).

Perfectionism and self-righteousness are a serious error.

“If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. … If we say that we haven’t sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.” (1 John 1:8, 10).

Indicator 5

  • Do you believe you are perfect, never doing anything wrong?
  • Do you consider yourself cleaner than most people?
  • Do you consider yourself acceptable to God only on the basis of your good deeds?

Indicator 6

  • Do you acknowledge that you are a sinner?
  • Do you feel sorrow when you do something wrong?
  • Do you fight against sinful habits in your life?
  • Do you feel that you are growing in your ability to overcome sin?
  • Are you overcoming temptation more and more?
  • Are you growing in obedience to the commandments?
  • Do you do these things only out of love and gratitude to God and to be like your beloved Lord Jesus Christ?

Indicator 7

  • Are you comfortable with things the Bible forbids as long as you manage to keep them secret?
  • Do you become bitter and furious against anyone who exposes you to an authority or in public?

Test results

Indicator 1: If you answered yes to all these questions, your test of belief is positive. God is your Father. All the answers must be positive; a single small negative puts your faith in Christ on sandy ground. You must belong entirely to Christ. If there are negatives, you must ask for help. You may lack teachers and understanding concerning the gospel. You may still have inner wounds and unforgiveness that block the witness of the Spirit of God with your spirit. That is why doubts remain in your mind.

Indicator 2: Positive answers to one or two of these questions show a lack of understanding of the gospel on your part. You need a good presentation of the gospel of Christ to properly establish your faith in Christ. Fortunately, you are in this class for that above all. If, on the other hand, you answer yes to all these questions, your test is negative. You are not a child of God. There is no doubt about it.

Indicator 3: “If we love one another,” says John in his first letter, “No one has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been perfected in us.” (4:12). “We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. He who doesn’t love his brother remains in death.” (3:14). The presence of love means the presence of the life of God in you. Love shows that you were born of God. He is your Father.

Indicator 4: If you answered yes to these two questions, even though the other parts of your test are positive, you need healing from certain wounds and past situations.

Indicator 5: If you answer yes to even one of these questions, you are not born of God, because God says you are a sinner and unable to save yourself, and you say the opposite. You have said that God is a liar. He is not your Father.

Indicator 6: If you value the commandments of God, if you grieve and confess when you break them, if something in you longs and strives to please God and be like Jesus, and if you are growing in obedience to God, then the behavior test is positive. God is your Father.

Indicator 7: If your answer is positive to one of these questions, you have a spiritual problem that you should think about mastering. If your answers to all these questions are positive, it must be said that your new birth leaves something to be desired. Only those who belong to the world live in darkness, take pleasure in shameful things and strive to keep them hidden, adding evil to evil. The children of God strive to do good and always want to come into the light. They want their works to be exposed, and they repent of their mistakes and wrongdoings.

If you generally have a positive test in the three levels, you are a child of God. You simply need to grow in your faith. We recognize that there may be places where you have answers that do not fit. That does not mean you are not a child of God or only a little bit a child of God. If the test overall shows more fitting answers, you are a child of God. As for the few negatives, you need to search the Scriptures to root your life in Christ more deeply.

If your spiritual DNA test is negative, it means you are not yet born of God. Here is what you must do: open yourself to God. You cannot be born again by what you do. It is up to God to give you birth. The only thing you can do is to stay before the Word of God, the real gospel. You must begin to know deeply God’s plan of salvation, what he accomplished in Jesus Christ, and to want salvation as a gift of God. Then you can confess with your mouth your faith in Jesus Christ as your Savior and Lord. Then God will make you his child by the sole action of his Holy Spirit. We must insist on the fact that God keeps his word. If you truly believe in Jesus Christ and confess with your mouth his Lordship and his Resurrection, the Holy Spirit immediately enters you, does the necessary cleaning in your spirit and settles inside as master. That is the new birth.

“For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.” (Rom 1:16). If we know the gospel and have accepted it, then we are born of God. But then, is it true that we know what the gospel is? Is it really what was preached to us? It is time to find out.

Gospel means GOOD NEWS.

“Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God’s Kingdom, and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”” (Mark 1:14-15). In this passage, the expressions “gospel” and “good news” translate the same Greek word: euaggelion. It is used to designate a good reward or information that gives joy, that is, good news. From this Greek word came the word “gospel”, which is the good news. Here we are speaking of the good news of the kingdom of God, which concerns what God has accomplished to save us in Jesus Christ. It is therefore the gospel of Jesus Christ (Mark 1:1, Gal 1:7). This gospel is announced by us. It is therefore our gospel (1 Thess 1:5). And since it is so dear to me, you will allow me to say that it is my gospel (Rom 16:25). Let us be proud of it, for it is the gospel of the glory of the blessed God (1 Tim 1:11). The joy and glory it produces for us and for those who receive it when we proclaim it are eternal, since the gospel itself is eternal (Rev 14:6).

The message of the gospel, the good news, is that God saves us in Jesus Christ with no contribution on our part other than faith. Here are Bible verses that clearly and briefly present our salvation by faith in Jesus Christ: Rom 3:23-24, Rom 5:6-8, Rom 4:25, 2 Cor 5:21, 1 Cor 15:1-5.

It can be summed up in a few lines as follows:

  • Everyone is a sinner
  • The penalty of sin is death (separation from God)
  • Heaven (the dwelling place of God) is a perfect place where only perfect people, that is, people without sin, are admitted
  • Man cannot become perfect by himself
  • Christ fully paid the ransom for our sins. He paid everything and offers us his righteousness
  • All man has to do is believe that the Lord Jesus Christ paid for all sins and accept him as Savior
  • We can be sure of having eternal life, because Jesus, who died to take away sin, rose again so that we may live forever through him

We have a sure salvation guaranteed by a living Savior! We must also share this salvation with those around us. We will come back to that. For the moment, let us move forward as far as we ourselves are concerned.

If you had doubts about your relationship with God, now is the time to sincerely accept God’s free gift of salvation by confessing Jesus Christ:

Lord Jesus Christ

I believed that I knew you. But now I realize how many times I need you.

I repent of all my sins. Forgive me all my sins. Have mercy on me. Come into my life.

I believe that you died on the cross to pay the penalty for my sins and rose on the third day for my justification.

I accept your grace and your salvation. I confess you as my Lord and my Savior. You saved me, I am saved.

Thank you, my Lord, for this great salvation. Amen!

After accepting the gospel by faith, it is essential to show your faith in the Lord through baptism by immersion. Baptism is not optional. It is essential to be saved. Refusing baptism amounts to rejecting Christ (Mark 16:15-16). After that, you must regularly take part in the Lord’s Supper (1 Cor 11:23-26) and live in fellowship with the brothers and sisters by taking part in the gatherings (Heb 10:23-25).

lecons.titre: Knowing how to enjoy the benefits of the covenant
lecons.html:
Jesus Christ, our Lord, guarantees us salvation. This salvation is a matter of covenant (Matt 26:26-28). It is a better covenant than anything God has ever made with a human being (Heb 7:22). And this covenant is established on better promises (Heb 8:6). Even more, it opens us to the possession of all the promises God made to the patriarchs in faith and which are confirmed in the prophets (2 Cor 1:20; Eph 2:12-13; 3:6).

Through Christ, we are heirs of God (Rom 8:16-17; Gal 3:26-29). We can therefore fully enjoy everything God possesses (1 Cor 3:23).

By making use of God’s promises, we come into possession of our rights and show our divine nature (2 Pet 1:3-4). These are the benefits of God’s Covenant with us through the blood of Jesus Christ.

We do this first by making firm decisions against the defilements of the flesh (2 Cor 7:1). That is, we are determined to be nothing less than the Bible’s description of our divine nature.

To do this, we take God at his word by faith, knowing that what God has said is what he does (Heb 6:12; Rom 4:19-21).

Because of this, we speak according to God to our personality, our body and soul, our circumstances and situations (Heb 10:24; Matt 21:21; 2 Cor 4:13).

By saying about ourselves what God has said, our being aligns itself with that Word. The Word of God is creative. What God says comes to pass. Just as he called light out of darkness simply by saying it, so he calls provision out of lack simply by saying it (2 Cor 4:6; Rom 4:17). Thus, what he said in the Bible is what we really are. Even if appearances say the opposite, and especially because of that, we must repeat the word of God constantly. Then it will produce in us the necessary dynamism, and our being, in some time, will be transformed into what is real.

It is not a matter of looking for special promises and verses in the Bible. You must eat everything; even what seem to be commandments are to be used by the Spirit and the power of the tongue to break the dominion of evil and impose light in us and around us. That way, the word of God stops being the problem or the headache and becomes the solution, the remedy, the landmark and the food.

You see, beyond statements like “God has blessed me with every spiritual blessing in Christ” and others, you can use the commandments of God to break the yokes of sin.

The law says: you shall not covet.

The one who is under the law says to himself, closing his eyes: “I must not covet.” But he keeps coveting, because the flesh makes him weak.

The one who is in Christ, relying on the grace of God, says to himself: “I cannot covet. God said I will not do it. That is why I do not covet…” Then, quite simply, his thoughts turn from covetousness to admiring creation and the goodness of God, and end in praise.

So take God at his word. Tell yourself that you are what he said, you have what he said, you do what he said. Say it, trusting him. The creative power of the Word will transform you before you realize it. This is how you arrive at the renewing of the mind.

lecons.titre: Being prepared for trials and persecutions
lecons.html:
Being a Christian, a child of God, is not synonymous with a life without challenges, trials and suffering. In fact, it is quite the opposite. Trials and persecutions are part of the Christian race.

Trials

A trial is a situation that comes to challenge your faith in spite of your integrity, your prayers and your sanctification. These are challenges that ordinary people meet. But these situations defy every solution of human wisdom that may be available to you. Moreover, they are challenges you have trouble overcoming even though you are serious about applying the divine principles explained in the Bible.

James says that when we find ourselves in such a situation, we should rejoice: “Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations,” (James 1:2) One may wonder why. For James, it is because “knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.” (James 1:3). Paul says he has made this a habit for the same reasons: “Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces perseverance;” (Rom 5:3). Peter also gives the same reasons for the presence of trials in the life of the Christian: “that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ—” (1 Pet 1:7).

It is with Peter that we understand more concretely what Paul and James tell us when they urge us to rejoice in trials. Peter shows that a trial is something that grieves (1 Pet 1:6). But when the child of God fixes his affection on Jesus Christ, even without seeing him physically, he finds within himself an inexpressible and glorious joy (1 Pet 1:8). So it is not the trial that is the object of our joy, nor the results to be produced in us, but the one who is with us in the midst of the trial, working on us to produce these good results: patience, perseverance, praise, glory and honor. The object of our joy is Jesus Christ.

The devil’s goal in stirring up people and the forces of nature to stand in our way and challenge us is to bring us to deny the faith. God’s goal in allowing these trials to come is to let our faith pass through the fire and shine brightly, so as to enlighten the world more and draw people to Jesus Christ. You see that it is truly reasonable to rejoice when we find ourselves facing situations that do not match our calculations and plans. We are facing a trial and God wants to give us a promotion. Even more, he is with us in the trial. He has measured it, made it match our capacity to resist, and has already decided to help us through it. It is already planned that you will pass the trial and receive the reward. You only have to look to the Master. “No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.” (1 Cor 10:13).

A trial may be an illness, financial difficulties, various embarrassments, disappointments, attacks on your reputation and more. And that already brings us to persecutions. For trials can come in the form of persecutions.

Persecutions and tribulations

Trials are simple situations that can happen to anyone but which, in our case, have a precise purpose. Persecutions, on the other hand, are directed at us by individuals intentionally. We must note that they are under the influence of the devil without knowing it. That is why, in spite of everything, we never take people as enemies. Persecutions are all the mistreatment we receive directly from people because we are children of God.

The presence of persecutions must not be a surprise to us. “strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.” (Acts 14:22). “Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.” (2 Tim 3:12). Our Lord has already assured us that this is unavoidable. “Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.” (John 15:20). This verse is just one swallow among many. The warnings of our Lord about persecutions and tribulations abound in the gospels (Matt 5:10-12; Mark 10:29-30; Luke 21:12).

However, persecutions must not be a reason for worry. Our Lord reassures us. “I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”” (John 16:33). “You will be handed over even by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends. They will cause some of you to be put to death. You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake. And not a hair of your head will perish. “By your endurance you will win your lives.” (Luke 21:16-19). Let us rejoice when we find ourselves in situations of trial. It is a blessing (James 1:1-5).

We are not, for this reason, invited to put ourselves in danger voluntarily in order to claim persecutions. That would be testing the Lord. Our Lord also teaches us that we must take precautions to ensure our own safety. The Lord’s order is: “But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you.” (Matt 10:17). This means making the necessary arrangements and finding out where we are going and how to share the good news with the people there without destroying ourselves through ignorance. Then, when we are caught, the Lord advises us to follow the direction of the Holy Spirit without panicking (Matt 10:17-22).

Our Lord even tells us to flee when the situation becomes very critical (Matt 10:23). This, however, is not to be done cowardly. We must show courage in proclaiming the good news. And above all, we must avoid at all costs denying the Lord in order to survive. It is better to lose life than the giver of life (Matt 10:28-33).

We must follow the example of our elders in the faith who, fleeing persecution in Jerusalem, ran with the gospel to other regions. They set things on fire wherever they went (Acts 8:1; Acts 11:19-21).

What exactly should we expect?

All kinds of bad reactions and treatment (Rom 8:35-39; 1 Peter 2:19-24).

Our reaction toward those who treat us badly must calmly be blessing (Rom 12:14).

We will also have to face difficulties of a natural kind, those things that happen to ordinary mortals, and face them with joy and faith in Christ (James 1:2-4).

Being persecuted for the name of Christ is an honor!

Christ requires each of his disciples to carry their cross and follow him: “He called the multitude to himself with his disciples, and said to them, “Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it.” (Mark 8:34-35).

But what does he really mean?

The cross, when you think about it, displays horrible, shameful and humanly unbearable suffering. That is indeed what it is:

“looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God. For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.” (Heb 12:2-3)

But the cross is not only suffering. It is also a solution. The cross is suffering for the one who carries it and a solution for one, if not several, other people:

“who didn’t sin, “neither was deceit found in his mouth.” When he was cursed, he didn’t curse back. When he suffered, he didn’t threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously. He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.” (1 Peter 2:22-24).

If the cross were only suffering, the world would welcome such an idea.

  • The innocent suffer for their ignorance.
  • Wrongdoers suffer the consequences of their misdeeds.
  • Great men suffer for their ideals.

If that were all there is to the vision of the cross of Christ, not only would the scandal of the cross be removed, but my salvation would be erased. That is inconceivable.

The cross of Christ is the power of God for salvation:

“For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the Good News—not in wisdom of words, so that the cross of Christ wouldn’t be made void. For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are dying, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.” (1 Cor 1:17-18).

If we keep this in mind, we will understand what our Lord tells us when he commands us to take up the cross and follow him.

“For what glory is it if, when you sin, you patiently endure beating? But if, when you do well, you patiently endure suffering, this is commendable with God. For you were called to this, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example, that you should follow his steps, who didn’t sin, “neither was deceit found in his mouth.” When he was cursed, he didn’t curse back. When he suffered, he didn’t threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously. He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.” (1 Peter 2:20-24)

To carry your cross is to lose your life for Christ and for the good news.

Let us look at the example of Paul:

  • He suffered a great deal (2 Tim 3:11)
  • But it was for the elect, for the church (Col 1:24)
  • It was above all in order to open more people to the salvation that is in Jesus Christ (1 Cor 9:19-27)

This is what we are called to.

We must not naively throw ourselves into trouble. We must not cause divisions out of boasting and then judge those who move away from us as persecutors. As far as it depends on us, we must be at peace with all people. But we must invest our time, our finances and our person in proclaiming the gospel, even at the risk of losing ourselves. Our struggle must be never to be an obstacle to the gospel, either by suffering through laziness and vice, or by fleeing suffering to the point of laying down too early the offensive and defensive weapons of righteousness.

“We give no occasion of stumbling in anything, that our service may not be blamed, but in everything commending ourselves, as servants of God, in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses, in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in watchings, in fastings; in pureness, in knowledge, in perseverance, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love, in the word of truth, in the power of God; by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left, by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true; as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and behold, we live; as punished, and not killed; as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things. Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians. Our heart is enlarged.” (2 Cor 6:3-11).

lecons.titre: Holding on to the hope of eternal life
lecons.html:
“If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.” (1 Cor 15:19).

We hope for provision to meet our temporary needs and to carry out our ministry effectively; but we may have to be content with the necessities.

“But having food and clothing, we will be content with that. But those who are determined to be rich fall into a temptation, a snare, and many foolish and harmful lusts, such as drown men in ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some have been led astray from the faith in their greed, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.” (1 Tim 6:8-10).

Let us remember who we are and fix our eyes on what matters for people of our rank:

“See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him. Beloved, now we are children of God. It is not yet revealed what we will be; but we know that when he is revealed, we will be like him; for we will see him just as he is. Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure.” (1 John 3:1-3).

  • There is a hope attached to God’s calling (Eph 1:18)
  • This hope must be a reason for joy for us in the midst of persecutions (Rom 12:12)
  • It is a sure hope that does not disappoint (Rom 5:5)
  • It is the hope of righteousness (Gal 5:5)
  • It is about the resurrection of the righteous (Acts 24:15)
  • We will then fully experience the glory of God (Rom 5:2)
  • Creation will be restored and our glorious identity revealed (Rom 8:19-25)
  • We will put on new and glorious bodies (Phil 3:20-21)

We await the return of our glorious Lord, the resurrection of our loved ones in the faith, the restoration of our bodies in the image of Christ’s, an eternity of happiness that cannot be compared to all the riches and luxuries of this world put together.

I cannot be satisfied with the miserable riches of this world; I prefer glory!

Jesus Christ said: “If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.” (John 8:36) So it is clear: we are free. If you have within you the Son of God Jesus Christ, you are free. And you have him as it is written: “For you are all children of God, through faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.” (Gal 3:26-27).

So you are free. But what have you been freed from? It is important to know in order to live freedom properly, and above all not to become a slave again if that were possible. We have been freed from everything that had triumphed over us, held us as slaves, and that we obeyed willingly or by force (2 Peter 2:19, John 8:34, Rom 6:16). We have been freed from the power and dominion of sin, of the devil, of dead works, of the guilty conscience, of men and their religious systems (Rom 6:20, Gal 2:4, Titus 1:14, Col 2:18-22, Heb 2:14-15, 9:14, 22). The Lord freed us from these things because they all join together to rot our existence and drive us by force toward eternal damnation.

The result of this freedom gained is that we can enter the presence of God at any time and without protocol (Eph 3:12, Heb 10:19). The freedom Christ has won for us is total, so that everything is permitted, truly everything. This means that whatever your life may be, access to the presence of God is always open to you, free and without protocol, through the blood of Jesus Christ that has already been shed. If anything claims that because of some fault we cannot go into the presence of God, it is completely wrong. If we happen to be caught off guard by sin and its schemes, it is directly into the presence of God that we go, daring to enter even Heaven itself if necessary, because that is where our advocate and our ransom is (1 John 2:1-2).

Let us know, however, that if we use the freedom given to us in any other way, as we said earlier, we can find ourselves a slave again. The apostle says: ““All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are expedient. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be brought under the power of anything. … Stand firm therefore in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and don’t be entangled again with a yoke of bondage.” (1 Cor 6:12, Gal 5:1). So stay free by living in righteousness (Rom 6:18), by acting as servants of God (1 Pet 2:16), by taking care not to make others stumble (1 Cor 8:9), and by avoiding becoming slaves of men even if they claim to be servants of God (1 Cor 7:23).

The experience of freedom must be made a reality every day. To do this, the child of God must each day:

  • Walk and pray in the Spirit (Rom 8:2, 2 Cor 3:6, 17, Jude 20-21)
  • Meditate on and practice the Word of God (John 8:32, John 17:17, Col 3:16)
  • Regularly bring all their needs to God in prayer with thanksgiving (Heb 4:16, Phil 4:6-7)
  • Act toward everyone in the love of Christ (Gal 5:13)

There are Christians who are intoxicated with grace. Or rather, it should be said that they are convinced of a message of grace that perhaps goes further than grace itself. As a child of God, you must remember that the freedom grace gives you is based on a law by which you will be judged (James 1:25, 2:12). “For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men, instructing us to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age; looking for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works.” (Titus 2:11-14)

So you are free to enter the presence of God if you understand that Christ has freed you from everything and everyone so that you become and remain his slaves through the practice of the righteousness and holiness of God (Rom 6:18-22). You can be as free as that, but no more. In any case, it is not possible to be freer than that. When you enter into Christ, you must live by his rules. Otherwise, you may return to your former slavery. But that would not reckon with Christ. He is not the kind to lose those whom his grace has touched.

lecons.titre: Understanding and carrying out your role as an ambassador of Christ
lecons.html:
Christ was on earth the representation of the whole Godhead. God was in Jesus Christ reconciling the world to himself. Christ has put in us the word of reconciliation. We therefore serve as ambassadors for Christ. What Christ did when he was physically on earth, what he would do if he were physically present today, it is up to us to do now.

We, whom God has reconciled to himself, we, who have become new creations in Christ by the action of God alone, we children of God, all of us, serve as ambassadors of Christ. Our mission is to reconcile people with God. Our message is: be reconciled to God. Our strategy is exhortation and pleading. We do not use force. We represent Christ; therefore we proclaim the message of the forgiveness of sins in the name of Jesus Christ, and we help people receive this forgiveness through repentance and faith. We heal the sick and set free the possessed and the oppressed by the anointing of the Holy Spirit (Acts 10:38).

We do this work, each one for their part according to the measure of grace, either as a special envoy or as a witness in our surroundings through a life that reflects the love, goodness and holiness of Christ.

The authority of Christ is conferred on us and we exercise it in his name (Phil 2:9-11). The authority given to us extends over demons, the forces of nature and our own body. We can and must therefore cast out demons, heal the sick and raise the dead in the name of Jesus Christ (Matt 10:8). But our authority does not touch the conscience and will of other human beings. We cannot therefore command them to receive Christ. That is why we plead with them and intercede for them in prayer. God alone can bend the human will without violating it.

All the needs of an ambassador are fully covered by the power he represents. In the Word of God, as ambassadors of Christ, we have the assurance of safety and full provision:

1. Safety in Christ: Ps 56:3-4, Proverbs 18:10, Ps 91:4, 2 Thess 3:3. To ensure our safety, the Lord covers us with his grace, honors us with his presence, comforts and warns us through the Holy Spirit within us, and assures us of a company of seasoned angels with precise orders. All that is required of us is prudence through the Holy Spirit to watch over our health and not foolishly put ourselves in danger.

2. God’s provision: Matt 6:31-33, Phil 4:19, 2 Cor 9:9-10. It is impossible that, while we follow God’s plan in our life and bear witness for Christ, we should lack means. If it should appear so, we must resist the enemy by faith and present our needs to God (James 4:7, Phil 4:6-7).

“Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God. For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.” (Heb 12:1-3)

“You therefore, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also. You therefore must endure hardship as a good soldier of Christ Jesus. No soldier on duty entangles himself in the affairs of life, that he may please him who enrolled him as a soldier. Also, if anyone competes in athletics, he isn’t crowned unless he has competed by the rules. The farmer who labors must be the first to get a share of the crops. Consider what I say, and may the Lord give you understanding in all things. Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, of the offspring of David, according to my Good News, in which I suffer hardship to the point of chains as a criminal. But God’s word isn’t chained. Therefore I endure all things for the chosen ones’ sake, that they also may obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory. This saying is trustworthy: “For if we died with him, we will also live with him. If we endure, we will also reign with him. If we deny him, he also will deny us. If we are faithless, he remains faithful; for he can’t deny himself.” Remind them of these things, charging them in the sight of the Lord, that they don’t argue about words, to no profit, to the subverting of those who hear. Give diligence to present yourself approved by God, a workman who doesn’t need to be ashamed, properly handling the Word of Truth.” (2 Tim 2:1-15)

Looking to his glory, Christ suffered the cross, despising its shame. Looking to the glory he offers us, let us suffer for the name of Christ and win the world for him. It is for the world that the Father gave his only Son. It is for the world that Christ suffered, died and rose again. It is the world that the Holy Spirit within us wants to convict. Let us take the world not for its riches but for salvation.

Let us go!

objectifs: You know with certainty whether or not you are a child of God.
You understand what being a disciple of Christ means day to day — not just an occasional believer.
You know and use your benefits in Christ.
You have made the Builder’s Identity Declaration your own.

qcm.e: The word comes from the Greek euaggelion: good news, information that gives joy.

qcm.q: According to the message of the Gospel, what is required on our part to be saved?
c: Works of charity in exchange for forgiveness
qcm.e: God saves us in Jesus Christ with no contribution other than faith (Romans 3:23-24).

qcm.q: According to the manual, a disciple of Christ is first of all…
c: A person born of God, who follows Christ and lives as he lived
Someone who goes to church regularly
Someone who simply believes in God
Someone who knows the whole Bible
qcm.e: See the introduction of the module (Luke 6:40).

qcm.q: According to 1 John 5:1, who is born of God?
c: The one who prays every day
Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ
The one who does good works
qcm.e: “Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God” (1 John 5:1).

qcm.q: What are the three tests presented to know whether one is a child of God?
qcm.e: The test of belief (faith), the test of attitude (love) and the test of action (holiness).

qcm.q: According to Paul, what becomes of the person who believes they are perfect and without sin?
c: They deceive themselves and the truth is not in them
They become a model for others
qcm.e: Perfectionism and self-righteousness are a serious error (1 John 1:8).

qcm.q: How do we take possession of the promises of the covenant?
c: By waiting for them to arrive without saying anything
By earning them through our good works
By taking God at his word by faith and saying about ourselves what God has said
qcm.e: The Word of God is creative: what God says comes to pass (Hebrews 6:12; 2 Corinthians 4:13).

qcm.q: How does the manual describe a “trial”?
c: A situation that challenges your faith despite your integrity, your prayers and your sanctification
The result of a hidden sin
A problem that good organization is enough to solve
qcm.e: See the lesson “Being prepared for trials and persecutions”.

qcm.q: Why does James (1:3) invite us to rejoice in trials?
c: Because they prove that we are perfect
Because the testing of faith produces endurance
qcm.e: “The testing of your faith produces endurance” (James 1:3).

qcm.q: According to Mark 8:34, what must the one who wants to follow Jesus do?
c: Wait for the trials to pass
Deny himself, take up his cross and follow him
Leave his job and his family
qcm.e: Carrying your cross is a daily and voluntary renunciation of yourself.

qcm.q: What does 1 Corinthians 15:19 say about the one who hopes in Christ for this life only?
c: He is the happiest of men
He is the most miserable of all men
qcm.e: The hope of eternal life keeps the disciple steady in the storm.

qcm.q: According to John 8:36, what happens when the Son sets free?
c: One is free only after death
One no longer has any rules
qcm.e: “If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.” (John 8:36).

qcm.q: What is the mission of the ambassador of Christ?
qcm.e: Our message: “Be reconciled to God”, through exhortation and pleading, without force.

qcm.q: How far does the authority of the ambassador of Christ extend?
c: Over demons, the forces of nature and our own body, but not over the will of other people
Over the will of those who refuse the Gospel
qcm.e: We cannot command people to receive Christ: we plead with them and intercede for them.

qcm.q: According to Romans 8:16-17, what have we become through Christ?
qcm.e: We are heirs of God and can enjoy the benefits of the covenant.

exercices.consigne: Answer each statement honestly with Yes or No. This test helps you discern the signs of authentic spiritual life. “Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him.” (1 John 5:1).

items: I believe the Word of the apostles (in the Bible) without reservation.
I believe the Bible without reservation.
I believe that Jesus is “the Christ”, “the Son of God” and “the true God and eternal life”.
I believe that Jesus “has come in the flesh” (in a human body) to die as “the atoning sacrifice for our sins” and “to destroy the works of the devil”.
I believe that Jesus Christ rose bodily from the dead.
I believe that Jesus is the only solution, the only savior of the world that God has given.
I believe that the Blood of Jesus Christ is enough to pay for my sins.
I believe that only because of Jesus, God forgives my sins and does not bring them up again.
I take delight in Jesus.
I trust in his love.
Jesus is enough for me.
In my opinion, Jesus was simply a good man, one wise man among many, a founder of a religion like any other, simply a great teacher, or a mere prophet.
I think that Jesus was not God.
I think that Jesus is not enough for me.
I think something must be added to faith in Christ.
I think it is possible to be right with God and have eternal life without Christ.
I love God.
I am excited by the things that relate to God and glorify him.
I love the people around me.
I love true Christians despite their differences from me.
I hate people for no reason.
I hate people just because of the color of their skin, their physical appearance, the way they laugh, etc.
I believe that I am perfect, never doing anything wrong.
I consider myself cleaner than most people.
I consider myself acceptable to God only on the basis of my good deeds.
I acknowledge that I am a sinner.
I feel sorrow when I do something wrong.
I fight against sinful habits in my life.
I feel that I am growing in my ability to overcome sin.
I overcome temptation more and more.
I am growing in obedience to the commandments.
I do these things only out of love and gratitude to God and to be like my beloved Lord Jesus Christ.
I am comfortable with things the Bible forbids when I manage to keep them secret.
I become bitter and furious against anyone who exposes me to an authority or in public.

indicateurs.t: Indicator 3 — Love for God and others

resultats: Indicator 1 — Faith in Christ — If you answered “Yes” to questions 1 to 11, your test of belief is positive. God is your Father. All the answers must be positive; a single small negative puts your faith in Christ on sandy ground. If there are negatives, you may lack teachers or understanding concerning the gospel, or you have inner wounds to be healed.

Indicator 2 — Understanding of the gospel — “Yes” answers to questions 12 to 16 show a lack of understanding of the gospel. You need a good presentation of the gospel of Christ. If you answer “Yes” to all these questions, your test is negative: you are not yet a child of God. Understanding and accepting the gospel is the prerequisite of life in Christ.

Indicator 3 — Love for God and others — If you answered “Yes” to questions 17 to 20, it reveals the presence of love in your life. “We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. He who doesn’t love his brother remains in death.” (1 John 3:14). Love shows that you were born of God.
Indicator 4 — Emotional wounds — If you answered “Yes” to questions 21 and 22, even though your test is otherwise positive, you need healing from certain wounds and past situations.

Indicator 5 — Self-righteousness — If you answer “Yes” to question 23, 24 or 25, there are strong doubts about your new birth. True repentance begins with acknowledging that you are a sinner. You are claiming the opposite of what God says about your condition as a sinner.

Indicator 6 — Fight against sin — If you answered “Yes” to questions 26 to 32, something in you longs to please God and you are growing in obedience. The behavior test is positive. God is your Father.

Indicator 7 — Attitude toward hidden sin — If you answer “Yes” to questions 33 and 34, you are seriously sick spiritually. The children of God strive to come into the light and repent of their mistakes.

CONCLUSION — If your Spiritual DNA test is positive, you are a child of God and simply need to grow in your faith. If the test is negative, you are not yet born of God — but God gives this birth to whoever desires it. Stay before his Word, discover the plan of salvation in Jesus Christ and confess your faith in him as Savior and Lord.

exercices.titre: Letter to God — my real spiritual situation
exercices.consigne: Write by hand, on a sheet of paper, a personal letter to God of at least one page. It is sincere and private: you do not have to hand it in. It must cover: where you really stand with God; the doubts or questions you do not dare to express at church; what you expect from this training. You will summarize your letter in the sheet.

champs.label: I wrote my letter to God (at least one page).

exercices.consigne: Learn the Builder’s Identity Declaration by heart. It is your main declaration: you will say it every morning and every evening, every day, until the end of your training. You will find it in the “Declaration” tab, with a reminder every day on your home page. You can move on to the rest of the course as soon as you have started.
exercices.intro_html:
I am (Your Name). I am a child of God in Christ.¹

The Lord my God is the one and true God.² I love the Lord my God with all my heart, with all my soul, with all my mind and with all my strength.³

The blessing of God is on me.⁴ I am not cursed and I cannot be.⁵

I am of the family of God.⁶ I love my brothers and sisters in Christ, and I know that they love me too, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who was given to us.⁷ I also love all people as myself. And I have the assurance that they cannot do me any harm. The Lord is with me.⁸

In all circumstances and situations, I remain calm, serene and confident in my God.⁹ He is my Father¹⁰ and he is in control of everything.¹¹ He makes all excellent grace abound toward me¹², he provides for my needs with riches and glory¹³, and he works all things together for my good.¹⁴ God is for me,¹⁵ and I am entirely God’s.¹⁶ All is well and all will always be well.

I have been crucified with Christ.¹⁷ The body of sin is dead.¹⁸ Now, all my faculties and members serve the righteousness of God.¹⁹ I have Jesus Christ as master and lord. I remain his property in the best and in spite of the worst.²⁰

The grace of God is fresh and abundant on me.²¹ I am strengthened by his almighty power.²² I have wisdom, knowledge, understanding and intelligence, for I have the mind of Jesus Christ.²³

I am led by the Holy Spirit.²⁴ I will not make a mistake.²⁵ I will not miss my target. The Holy Spirit leads me by the brightness of his light on my path.²⁶

I am clothed with the garments of salvation. I am covered with the robe of righteousness.²⁷ My God establishes me by the fragrance of his presence.²⁸ I am a wonder and a marvel²⁹, because I am a bearer of the glory of God.³⁰

I walk in power.³¹ I walk in authority.³² I walk in dominion.³³ I impact my world exceptionally.³⁴ I advance as a conqueror in the mighty name of Jesus Christ.³⁵
